SCREENSHOT - Cmdr - Personal use only - SCREENSHOT
More fixes than new things this time. The most interesting new things:
• Copying thousands of small files onto a local disk got many times faster. It's
always a compromise between speed and data safety, but the old balance
was way too conservative. Transfers are now a lot faster, and Cmdr still
makes sure every file is safely on the drive before it reports "done".
• The Operation log got a lot more useful: if you did something silly, you can
now properly review and roll back your copy, move, or trash operation, in
whole or in part. Even days later.
• If a volume suddenly becomes unavailable mid-transfer (typically a NAS
reboot or a router restart), the file now carries on from where it was once the
share is back: this applies to downloads from SMB, SFTP, NFS, S3, and
WebDAV, and to uploads to SMB.
